{{Short description|Solvable form of differential equation}}
{{Multiple issues|{{more footnotes needed|date=October 2016}}{{lead too short|date=October 2016}}{{how-to|date=October 2016}}{{technical|date=October 2016}}}}
{{Differential equations}}

An '''inexact differential equation''' is a [[differential equation]] of the form:

: <math>M(x,y) \, dx+N(x,y) \, dy=0 </math>

satisfying the condition

: <math>\frac{\partial M}{\partial y} \ne \frac{\partial N}{\partial x} </math>

[[Leonhard Euler]] invented the [[integrating factor]] in 1739 to solve these equations.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.eoht.info/page/History+of+differential+equations|title=History of differential equations – Hmolpedia|website=www.eoht.info|access-date=2016-10-16}}</ref>

== Solution method ==
To solve an inexact differential equation, it may be transformed into an [[exact differential|exact differential equation]] by finding an [[integrating factor]] <math>\mu</math>.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://people.clas.ufl.edu/cmcyr/files/2.5-Notes.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com|title=Special Integrating Factors|website=people.clas.ufl.edu|access-date=2025-02-08}}</ref> Multiplying the original equation by the integrating factor gives:

: <math>\mu M\,dx+\mu N\,dy=0</math>.

For this equation to be exact, <math>\mu</math> must satisfy the condition:

: <math display="inline">\frac{\partial\mu M}{\partial y}=\frac{\partial\mu N}{\partial x}</math>.

Expanding this condition gives:

:<math>M\mu_y-N\mu_x+(M_y-N_x)\mu = 0.</math>

Since this is a [[partial differential equation]], it is generally difficult. However in some cases where <math>\mu</math> depends only on <math>x</math> or <math>y</math>, the problem reduces to a [[separable differential equation|separable]] [[first-order linear differential equation]]. The solutions for such cases are:
:<math>\mu(y)=e^{\int{\frac{N_x-M_y}{M} \, dy}}</math>
or
:<math>\mu(x)=e^{\int{\frac{M_y-N_x}{N} \, dx}}.</math>
